the mineralization process is a complex and dynamic process that involves cellular uptake, intracellular accumulation, and release of Ca2+‐Pi complexes, which are the initial components of the mineral phase of the calcifying extracellular matrix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth plate chondrocye is a dynamic and highly specialized cell that has a unique role in the development and maintenance of skeletal tissues.

mineralization of the extracellular matrix is a multistep process that involves: 1. cellular uptake of Ca ^{2+} and Pi, 2. formation of complexes of calcium phosphate, membrane phospholipids, and proteins within intracellular vesicles, 3. formation of matrix vesicles by fusion of these intracellular vesicles with the plasma membrane, and 4. transformation of these matrix vesicles into mineralized clusters of crystalline hydroxyapatite.
mineralizing growth plate cells accumulate large amounts of intracellular Ca and Pi, which are then released as cell blebs, which are the precursors of mineral deposits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chondrocyte is the cell that is responsible for mineralization of the matrix in the growth plate.
mineralization of the extracellular matrix is initiated by the chondrocyte itself.
chondrocyte mineralization is a highly organized process.
